hook: A tangle of yarn that plays notes and hands out little gifts sounds like the gentlest thing in the archive. Glance at the odd object class line before you start: it is a small joke, and it also warns you that the file has two halves. Read it as a before-and-after story and notice exactly where the mood turns.
whyItMatters: The page carries a rewrite tag, so what you read is a reworked version of an older entry. It also sits under its own 'eric' tag, named after someone the text mentions constantly and never explains. That withheld identity is the whole hook: a toy-like object with an attachment to a person the reader never meets.
thingsToNotice:
The early effects read like a children's party, with a kitten, a safety-minded song and a birthday treat. After the scissors incident the effects stay in the same families but turn hostile, so the second list works as a dark mirror of the first. The trigger is tiny: one attempt to cut it, one question, one wrong answer.

Also compare the two containment paragraphs. The jump from a deposit box and request forms to a reinforced box swapped out by a robotic arm in seconds says more about the change than any description of the object.

related.note: Another dispenser of small treats whose output sours when misused.
A famous ask-and-receive machine; compare how each file plays with randomness.
